8: Three early writings keep sayings that belong beside the Beatitudes. The colour marks are those of the Thomas sayings: green agrees with the Qur’an, blue is beyond the measure, gold is unclear. Sayings left out are listed, each with its reason, on the page of early writings set aside.

- [agree] 1 Clement 13:2. Be merciful, so that you obtain mercy. Forgive, so that you are forgiven. As you do, so it will be done to you; as you judge, so you will be judged; as you show kindness, so kindness will be shown to you. The measure you give is the measure you receive.{{fn:1 Clement 13:1-2 (Roberts and Donaldson), where Clement calls it “the words of the Lord Jesus which He spake, teaching us meekness and long-suffering”. It blends Matthew 5:7, 6:14-15 and 7:1-2 with Luke 6:36-38, so it witnesses to those sayings and adds none. Agrees with Qur’an 24:22, which tells believers to pardon and overlook so that God may forgive them, and with 42:40. The Didache teaches the same mercy at 1:3-5.}}

- [agree] Epistle of the Apostles 18. Love your enemies, and do to no one what you would not want done to you.{{fn:Epistle of the Apostles 18 (James, 1924). The Epistle sets the words after “a new commandment: love one another”, in a farewell it places after the resurrection. That setting is not kept (Qur’an 4:157); the saying is. Compare Matthew 5:44 and 7:12; Luke 6:27 and 31. Agrees with Qur’an 41:34, which says to repel evil with what is better, so that the one who was an enemy becomes a close friend. The Didache has the same teaching at 1:2-4: the golden rule, a blessing for those who curse you, prayer for your enemies, the other cheek, the second mile, a gift to everyone who asks.}}

- [agree] Gospel of Mary, page 10. Where the mind is, there is the treasure.{{fn:Gospel of Mary, page 10 (Mattison), spoken to Mary in a vision, which is not kept. Compare Matthew 6:21 and Luke 12:34, where the word is “heart”. Agrees with Qur’an 26:88-89: on the Day, wealth and children avail nothing except for the one who comes to God with a sound heart.}}
9: One saying from Barnabas belongs here. The marks are as above.

- [agree] Epistle of Barnabas 5:9. I came to call sinners to repentance, and not the righteous.{{fn:Barnabas 5:9 (Roberts and Donaldson), quoting Matthew 9:13; Mark 2:17; Luke 5:32. Agrees with Qur’an 39:53, where God tells those who have wronged themselves not to despair of His mercy, and with 3:135. Barnabas adds that Jesus chose apostles “who were sinners above all sin”. That claim is not kept: the Qur’an calls the disciples helpers of God who believed and submitted (3:52; 61:14), and no gospel says the Twelve were sinners above all others.}}
13: The Gospel of Mary, the Epistle of the Apostles and the Didache each bear on the mission of the Twelve.

- [unclear] Gospel of Mary, pages 8 and 9. Preach the gospel of the kingdom. Lay down no rules beyond what I have given you, and do not make a law like the lawgiver, or you will be bound by it.{{fn:Gospel of Mary, pages 8 and 9 (Mattison), the close of the Savior’s farewell. The first two commands fit Qur’an 3:50 and 5:46-47: Jesus confirms what came before him, and the People of the Gospel are to judge by what God sent down in it. The third is unclear. If “the lawgiver” is Moses, the words cannot mean that the Torah is dropped, since 5:46 says the Injīl confirms it. If they forbid any later maker of rules, they agree with 9:31. The sense is open, so the mark is gold.}}

- [agree] Epistle of the Apostles 24 and 46. Keep my commandments. Turn your face from no one, and fear no one, the rich least of all. Serve on the way that is direct and narrow, without regard for a person’s rank.{{fn:Epistle of the Apostles 24 and 46 (James). Compare Matthew 7:13-14. Agrees with Qur’an 3:50-51, where Jesus says to fear God and obey him, because God is his Lord and theirs, and that this is a straight path; with 33:39, which praises those who convey God’s messages and fear none but God; and with 4:135 on standing for justice whether the party is rich or poor.}}

- [agree] Didache, title and 9:2-3. The Didache is headed “The Lord’s Teaching through the Twelve Apostles”, and its prayers thank the Father “through Jesus Your Servant”.{{fn:Didache, title, 9:2-3 and 10:2 (Riddle). The Greek for “Servant” is pais, the word Acts 3:13 and 4:27 use of Jesus. Agrees with Qur’an 4:172, where the Messiah does not disdain to be a servant of God, and with 19:30. The thanksgiving over the broken bread names “life and knowledge” made known through Jesus, and says nothing of a body given or blood shed for sins. This item is a note and not a saying of Jesus.}}
18: Two more early witnesses speak to the little ones and to correcting a brother.

- [agree] 1 Clement 46:8. Woe to the man who causes one of my chosen to stumble. It would be better for him never to have been born, or to have a millstone hung about his neck and be sunk in the sea, than to cause one of my little ones to stumble.{{fn:1 Clement 46:7-8, opened with “Remember the words of our Lord Jesus Christ”. Clement joins Matthew 18:6-7 and 26:24 with Mark 9:42 and Luke 17:1-2, so this is a witness to those sayings. Agrees with Qur’an 16:25 and 29:13: those who lead others astray carry their own burdens and some of the burdens of those they led astray.}}

- [agree] Epistle of the Apostles 48 and 49. If you see a brother sin, correct him between you and him. If he does not hear you, take two or three more. Give no credit to a report against your brother, do not spread slander, and take no pleasure in hearing it.{{fn:Epistle of the Apostles 48-49 (James); the Coptic breaks off in the middle of chapter 48, and the rest follows the Ethiopic. Matthew 18:15-17 has the procedure, and the Didache cites it at 15:3 (“as you have it in the Gospel”). Agrees with Qur’an 3:104 and 3:110, on calling to what is right and forbidding what is wrong, and with 49:6 and 49:12, which tell believers to verify reports and not to backbite.}}
21: The Didache, a church manual of the late first or early second century, opens with the same two commandments as this section.{{fn:Didache 1:2 (Riddle): “First, you shall love God who made you; second, your neighbour as yourself.” It gives them as the way of life, and it ends its teaching with no word of atonement. Agrees with Qur’an 4:36: worship God, join nothing with Him, and do good to parents, relatives and neighbours.}}
22: Two sayings warn of the few who answer the call and of those who bend the Scripture.

- [agree] Epistle of Barnabas 4:14. Many are called, but few are chosen.{{fn:Barnabas 4:14 (Roberts and Donaldson), which quotes the words as “written”. Compare Matthew 22:14. Agrees with Qur’an 12:103 (most people will not believe, however much you wish it) and 34:13 (few of God’s servants are grateful).}}

- [agree] Epistle of the Apostles 29 and 50. Whoever teaches another doctrine, bends the Scripture and adds to it to gain glory, and so makes believers fall, will be punished. Another doctrine will come, and woe to those who falsify my word and command.{{fn:Epistle of the Apostles 29 and 50 (James). Agrees with Qur’an 2:79, which pronounces woe on those who write the book with their own hands and say “this is from God”, with 3:78 and with 5:13. The Epistle adds that “it must needs be” that good and evil are made manifest; compare Matthew 18:7 and Qur’an 29:2-3.}}
24: The early writings carry more of the farewell speech than any other section draws on. Their sayings are set here in the order of their sources.

- [agree] Epistle of Barnabas 7:11. Those who wish to see me and take hold of my kingdom must receive me through hardship and suffering.{{fn:Barnabas 7:11 (Roberts and Donaldson). No gospel carries these words. Barnabas uses them to read the wool among thorns on the scapegoat as a type of the passion; that reading assumes the crucifixion and is not kept (Qur’an 4:157). The words agree with 2:214, which says Paradise is not entered without the trials that came on those before, and with 29:2-3.}}

- [agree] Epistle of the Apostles 36. Affliction is a proving, to show whether you have faith, remember my sayings and keep my commandments.{{fn:Epistle of the Apostles 36 (James). Agrees with Qur’an 2:155 and 29:2-3. The Epistle says this of a coming pestilence; the words stand without it.}}

- [agree] Epistle of the Apostles 27. If anyone believes in me and does not keep my commandments, though he confesses my name, he gains nothing and runs a vain race.{{fn:Epistle of the Apostles 27 (James). Compare Matthew 7:21-23 and Luke 6:46. Agrees with Qur’an 61:2-3, which asks why believers say what they do not do, and with 3:50, where obedience is the point. The same chapter has Jesus preach in the place of the dead and pour out forgiveness; that part is set aside, with the reason, on the page of early writings set aside.}}

- [agree] Epistle of the Apostles 29. Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed.{{fn:Epistle of the Apostles 29 (James); compare John 20:29, which the Diatessaron carries in its harmony. The Epistle gives the saying to a risen Jesus, and that scene is not kept (Qur’an 4:157). The words agree with 2:3, which praises those who believe in the unseen, and with 21:49 and 67:12.}}

- [agree] Epistle of the Apostles 24 and 25. The resurrection of the flesh will come, with the soul and the spirit. What has fallen will rise again, what was lost will be found, and what was weak will be restored.{{fn:Epistle of the Apostles 24-25 (James). The chapter ends “as he hath done unto me, so will I do unto all that believe in me”; that clause assumes Jesus died and was raised from the grave, and is not kept (4:157). The rest agrees with Qur’an 36:78-79 and 75:3-4, where the one who asks who will give life to decayed bones is told that He who created them the first time will do it.}}

- [agree] Epistle of the Apostles 39. Every person has the power to believe in the light and live, or to turn from it. No one will have a defence on that day who confessed the light and did the works of darkness.{{fn:Epistle of the Apostles 39 (James). The speech goes on to say “which Son am I” and “I am the word: I became flesh”; those clauses are set aside on the page of early writings set aside. The words kept agree with Qur’an 18:29 (let whoever wills believe, and whoever wills disbelieve) and 76:3.}}

- [beyond] Epistle of the Apostles 34 to 37. Before the end there will be signs in the sky, drought, pestilence and war, and believers will be persecuted. Many who bear my name will follow evil and teach vain doctrine, and the rich will be honoured above the faithful.{{fn:Epistle of the Apostles 34-37 (James). The Qur’an names its own signs of the Hour (21:96; 27:82; 44:10) and none of these. The Epistle’s list neither adds to them nor denies them, so it is beyond the measure. The warning about those who bear the name and follow evil agrees with 61:2-3.}}

- [unclear] Gospel of Mary, page 8. Peace be with you. Acquire my peace. Take care that no one leads you astray by saying “Look here” or “Look there”. The Son of Humanity exists within you. Follow him, for those who seek him will find him.{{fn:Gospel of Mary, page 8 (Mattison). “Look here, look there” has parallels in Luke 17:21-23 and Matthew 24:23, which fit the warnings of this section. Mattison’s note says “Son of Humanity” is an idiom for “human”, which suits a Messiah who is the son of Maryam and a human messenger (5:75). “Exists within you” is unclear: Luke 17:21 says the kingdom is “within” or “among” you, and translators divide. Peace on Jesus is in 19:33. The Gospel of Mary puts the words after a resurrection; that setting is not kept. Marked gold.}}

- [agree] Diatessaron, Section XLVI (John 14:28). My Father is greater than I.{{fn:Tatian’s Diatessaron, about 170 CE, Section XLVI (Hogg, in Ante-Nicene Fathers 9); the work survives in an Arabic translation of a Syriac text, and Hogg’s English follows the Arabic. The earliest harmony of the four gospels carries the words, so they were in the gospels before it was made. Agrees with Qur’an 5:72, where the Messiah says to worship God, his Lord and theirs, and with 4:172.}}

- [agree] Diatessaron, Section LIII (John 20:17). I ascend to my Father and your Father, and to my God and your God.{{fn:Tatian’s Diatessaron, Section LIII (Hogg). The setting is Mary Magdalene at the tomb, which assumes a risen Jesus and is not kept; the words stand. They agree with Qur’an 5:72 and 19:36, where Jesus says that God is his Lord and theirs. “Father” is read as on the page of Thomas sayings set aside: the phrase puts Jesus and the disciples in the same relation to God.}}

The Didache closes with the same warning to watch.{{fn:Didache 16:1 (Riddle): “Watch for your life’s sake. Let not your lamps be quenched, nor your loins unloosed; but be ready, for you know not the hour in which our Lord comes.” Compare Matthew 24:42 and 25:1-13. Agrees with Qur’an 7:187 and 33:63: the knowledge of the Hour is with God alone.}}
